analysis.investment_thesis: Unified Data-Tech is a tiny Rs 619 Cr IT services firm with a disastrous ROE of 0.36% yet trading at P/E 21 — earnings quality is essentially absent. This fails my most basic quality filter; I prefer boring consumer compounders with 18-22% ROE, not sub-1% ROE IT microcaps.
key_strengths: Promoter holding healthy at 60.39%, above my 55% threshold
No obvious leverage concerns visible at this market cap
P/E of 21 not extreme in absolute terms
key_risks: ROE of 0.36% — the business earns almost nothing on its capital
IT-ES is outside my circle of competence and highly commoditized
Microcap at Rs 619 Cr with negligible institutional interest (FII 0.57%)
red_flags: ROE near zero contradicts the 21x P/E — paying growth multiple for no profitability
Minimal DII/FII ownership signals lack of institutional validation
No visible dividend track record or multi-year earnings consistency data
analysis.detailed_analysis:
My investment framework demands predictable, high-quality businesses with ROE north of 15% and preferably 18-22% for core holdings. Unified Data-Tech's 0.36% ROE is simply incompatible with my standards — a business that cannot earn even 1% on shareholder equity has no moat and no pricing power, regardless of how the PE optically looks. At 21x earnings, the market is paying a reasonable-business multiple for sub-par economics, which is the classic value trap in microcap IT.

I build my wealth in retail and FMCG because demand is predictable and working capital cycles are tight. A 15-year-old IT-ES shop with Rs 619 Cr market cap competing against TCS, Infosys, and thousands of others is neither defensible nor within my circle. Promoter holding at 60.39% is the only tick mark, but governance signals alone don't compensate for near-zero profitability. I would pass without a second look and continue hunting steady consumer compounders.
